name_reason: Compliant with the fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention and consistent with every sibling in chevt1.c (handler_00..handler_2e). The '18' is the dispatch-table index (idx 0x18 of the per-event handler table at 0x51B91; entry at 0x51BF1 = 0x51B91 + 0x18*4 holds this function's address 0x000348fc) -- a meaningful domain ID, not a Ghidra address residue (the function address 0x348FC does not end in 18). '__unref' is accurate: the only xref is the data dispatch table (from 0x51BF1), 0 direct callers, and no chapter FDFIELD turn-event/tile-step hook dispatches this slot. '__dialog' is accurate: the body is a minimal dialog-only beat.
purpose: Unreferenced dispatch-table slot idx 0x18: a minimal dialog-only chapter event handler that shows chapter-text dialog page 3 and returns.
logic_summary: Straight-line, no-branch. After the compiler-injected __CHK(0x28) stack probe, it calls fd2_display_dialog_scene(data_fd2_current_chapter_text, page=3, 0xA0000 VGA base, 0x140 stride, 0xCD/0x4C window X/Y, 0x4A style, 0x13 max lines, 1 wait-for-input) and returns. No portrait reload, no camera pan, no global state writes, no RNG, no numeric computation; the dialog call's return value is discarded. In the original binary the body is PUSH 0x28; CALL __CHK, then falls through into the 8-PUSH chain at 0x34906 (also the named helper fd2_show_chapter_intro_text_dialog_mode_3) which JMPs (0x3491F -> 0x34C0F) into the shared tail of fd2_show_chapter_dialog_with_portrait_set_1 (PUSH data_fd2_current_chapter_text; CALL fd2_display_dialog_scene; ADD ESP,0x24; RET). It also exposes a Class-3 shared entry at 0x34901 (the CALL __CHK instruction) that fd2_chapter_event_handler_22 @ 0x34C6C borrows via PUSH 0x28; JMP 0x34901, reusing this entire body. Reproduced as a single inline dialog call for Layer-2 equivalence.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: The uniform per-event dispatch argument from the handler table at 0x51B91 (1-arg cdecl). The body never reads it.
params.reason: Descriptive of the uniform dispatch-table arg, no address residue. The body does not consume it, so a more specific name is not warranted; matches the convention used across sibling handlers in chevt1.c.

returns.semantics: No return value (void). fd2_display_dialog_scene's uint32 return is discarded.
